long_biography.plain_text:
A prototype for unloading freight containers caught Wim Bosman’s attention after decades running a logistics business. He invested in Copal, supplying finance and technical experience to help develop its machinery. His contribution also included introducing the company’s entrepreneurs to contacts in the transport industry, giving the venture access to his professional network.

The appeal lay in a familiar workplace problem: unloading containers still involved heavy manual labour. Copal’s machines could remove cargo and place it on pallets, reducing the physical demands on warehouse staff. Bosman supported technology that could make this work easier for older employees and help them remain in employment longer.

uncertainties.detail: Bosman died in 2017. Primary industry and wealth relationship describe his late-life interests, not a living role. Bonita’s present property list is not backdated; Copal participation and Bonita chairmanship are independently tied to his lifetime.

Father’s transport business supplied family industry context, but inheritance, seed capital, substantial mentoring or other materially decisive support are not established. Broad self-made rests on separate founder ownership and sale, not absence of inheritance. An advantaged-start subtype was considered but not assigned merely from parental occupation.

The source age 76 with a 2020 timestamp is stale, matching age at death in 2017. System-calculated age fields are not proposed. Full name and birth date come from local historical scholarship corroborated by the exact Dutch encyclopedia and company life years; no additional nationality found.
